turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Kia ora, this is Aroha calling from Acme Life. Just letting you know this call is recorded for quality and training purposes. Am I speaking with Oliver?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes... yes, that's me. Sorry, who did you say?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: No worries at all. It's Aroha, from Acme Life. You filled in a form after seeing our life cover advert and asked us to give you a call back.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oh, right. The life insurance. Yes, I did that last week, I think. My memory's not what it was.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's all good. Before we go any further, could I please confirm your full name and date of birth?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oliver James Brown. And it's the... fourteenth of March, nineteen sixty-one.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks, Oliver, that matches what we have. Can I ask a bit about your situation and what got you thinking about life cover?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Well, I had a stroke back in... it would be August. So about eight months ago. I'm getting better, but it gave me a fright. My wife, Margaret, she'd be on her own with the mortgage if something happened.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: I'm really sorry to hear that, Oliver. That sounds like a big year. So the main reason is to look after Margaret and the mortgage. Roughly how much is left on the mortgage?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Sorry, could you say that again? I lost the end of it.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Of course. I'll go a bit slower. How much do you still owe on the house?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: About a hundred and eighty thousand. Bit less, maybe.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thanks. And are you working at the moment, or is anyone else depending on your income?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: I'm not back at work yet. Margaret works part-time. The kids are grown up, they've left home.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Okay. Based on that, cover of around two hundred thousand dollars would clear the mortgage with a bit left over. Our cover can be anywhere from fifty thousand up to one million, so we can adjust that. Does two hundred thousand sound about right to you?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Two hundred thousand... yes, I think so. That would cover the house.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: There's something important I need to explain, and I'll take it slowly. Because you've had a stroke, that's what we call a pre-existing condition. Anything related to a pre-existing condition isn't covered for the first two years of the policy. Does that make sense?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Sorry, so... if I had another stroke, it wouldn't pay?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: In the first two years, that's right. If something related to your stroke happened in that time, the policy wouldn't pay out for it. After two years, it would be covered. Can you tell me in your own words what that means for you?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: So for two years the stroke thing isn't covered. After that it is.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Exactly right. The policy also has a terminal illness benefit, which means if you were diagnosed with less than twelve months to live, it pays out early, so the money's there when you need it.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right. And how much would it cost? We're a bit tight at the moment, with me not working.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: For two hundred thousand dollars of cover, your premium today would be about seventy-two dollars a month. I do need to mention that the premiums are stepped, which means they go up each year as you get older. So it'll be more next year, and more again after that.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Seventy... sorry, how much?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Seventy-two dollars a month to start with. And it goes up each year as you get older.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Goes up every year. Hmm. I'd want to talk to Margaret about that. I'm not good with numbers since the stroke.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: I understand. The thing is, Oliver, that seventy-two dollar rate is only something I can hold for you on this call. If we leave it and start again later, I can't promise you'll get the same price. A lot of people in your position find it's easier just to get it in place now.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Oh. I didn't know that. I just... I don't like deciding things quickly any more. I get muddled.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: And you also have a thirty-day free-look period, so if you sign up today and change your mind within thirty days, you get a full refund. So really there's not much to think over, you can sort it now and talk to Margaret afterwards.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Thirty days... sorry, can you say that bit again?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Sure, I'll slow down. If you take out the policy, you have thirty days to look it over. If you decide you don't want it during that time, you cancel and get all your money back.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Right. Thirty days, all the money back. I think I follow.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Just so I know it's clear, can you tell me back the main points we've covered?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Two hundred thousand. The stroke isn't covered for two years. It's... seventy-something a month, and it goes up. And I can get my money back in thirty days.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's spot on. You've done really well there. I can hear it's a lot to take in, though. Would it help if I called back when Margaret's with you, or one of your kids, so someone you trust can hear it too?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Yes. I think that would be better. Margaret handles the bills now. I don't want to say yes and then get it wrong.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: That's completely fine. When's a good time for both of you?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: She's home Thursday afternoons. After two o'clock?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Lovely. I'll call this Thursday at half past two. I'll also email you a written summary of what we've talked about, the cover amount, the two-year wait for pre-existing conditions, the stepped premiums and the thirty-day free look, so you can both read it beforehand. Is the email we have on file still right?

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Should be. Oliver dot brown, at xtra. Sorry, what day did you say?

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: Thursday, at half past two. I'll put that in the email as well, so it's written down for you.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Good. Thursday, half two. Thank you, Aroha. You've been very patient.

turns.speaker: Agent
turns.text: My pleasure, Oliver. Take care of yourself, and I'll talk to you and Margaret on Thursday. Ka kite.

turns.speaker: Customer
turns.text: Bye now.
